ablations.prompt: Explain inflation to a 10-year-old. Use simple words. Make sure a child could understand it.

runs.answer:
Imagine you have $5, and you go to the store to buy a candy bar that costs $5. You can buy it, and you have no money left.

Now imagine that next year, the same candy bar costs $6. Your $5 can't buy it anymore. Nothing happened to your money. It's still $5. But the candy bar got more expensive.

That's inflation. Inflation means things get more expensive over time, so your money can buy less than it could before.

Why does this happen? Sometimes lots of people want to buy things, but there isn't quite enough to go around. Stores can raise their prices, and the people who make the candy might need more money for sugar and workers, so the price goes up.

Grown-ups keep an eye on inflation. If prices go up just a little bit each year, that's normal and usually okay. If they go up too fast, it becomes hard for families to afford the things they need, like food and clothes.

So inflation is like the price tags growing a little bigger each year, and your money has to work a little harder to keep up.

Imagine you have $5, and at the corner store, a candy bar costs $1. You can buy five candy bars with your money.

Now imagine that next year, the same candy bar costs $2. Your $5 still looks the same, but now it only buys two candy bars. Your money didn't change, but the candy got more expensive. That's inflation.

Inflation means that prices go up over time. Things like candy, toys, food, and bikes cost a little more each year. Because of this, each dollar you have can buy a little less than it could before.

Why do prices go up? Sometimes lots of people want to buy the same things, and stores raise their prices. Sometimes it costs more to make things, like when the ingredients for candy get more expensive. And sometimes there's just more money floating around, so each dollar becomes worth a bit less.

Grown-ups usually think of inflation as a little bit of price growth each year, not a huge jump all at once. A small amount is normal and happens in most places.

So the big idea is this: inflation is when your money slowly buys less stuff than it used to, because prices keep creeping up.
